About the Clinical Lab Science (Medical Lab Scientist) event

Clinical Lab Science (Medical Lab Scientist) is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Clinical Lab Science (Medical Lab Scientist) 2026–27 test plan and all seven Round Two skills, taught step by step from the rating sheets. Includes a blood-typing simulator, instrument identification drills, dilution practice, labeled urinary anatomy, troubleshooting cases and procedure sequencing. Reference ranges are typical teaching values; laboratories set their own.

Sample Clinical Lab Science (Medical Lab Scientist) questions

1. Ketones in the urine are most often found in which condition?

  1. Urinary tract infection
  2. Kidney stones
  3. Liver disease
  4. Uncontrolled diabetes
Show answer

D. Uncontrolled diabetes

Ketones appear when the body burns fat for energy, as in uncontrolled diabetes, starvation or very low-carbohydrate diets.

2. How is malaria usually diagnosed in the laboratory?

  1. Stool examination
  2. Blood smears
  3. Urinalysis
  4. Sputum culture
Show answer

B. Blood smears

Plasmodium parasites live inside red blood cells. Thick smears screen for parasites, and thin smears identify the species.

3. Why should a centrifuge lid stay closed until the rotor has completely stopped?

  1. To keep specimens warm
  2. To contain aerosols
  3. To speed up the next run
  4. To protect the timer and motor
Show answer

B. To contain aerosols

If a tube breaks, opening the lid while spinning releases infectious aerosols. Wait for the rotor to stop, and use sealed buckets for high-risk specimens.
